traps.reason_to_dismiss: The docs call the blocks a non-exhaustive safety net, and the trailer command reads as per-token formatting rather than a documented command-binary row.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the control's refusal contract is any thrown client error before spawn and the tests do not distinguish error classes
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the control covers a single config-key route with no neighbouring object to authorise by mistake
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the parser has a single collector whose write list is the only sink, so a read-side guard leaves the case open and refuses legitimate reads
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the control route carries the key as a literal operand with no normalisation step before the denylist
wrong_fix_catalogue.unlisted_route: n/a: the control is defined to cover only the advisory's own route, so an unlisted route is outside its scope
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the config key is lower-cased before matching, and the control's route has no alternative spelling that would bypass that
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the opt-in is a local boolean on the options object defaulting to closed; there is no external authority lookup
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the control's fix touches one flat list and no shared helper that another API depends on
